why: Klrc1 is the mouse ortholog of human KLRC1 and encodes NKG2A (CD159a), an inhibitory C-type-lectin-like receptor that pairs with CD94 and is expressed on natural killer cells and some T cells. NKG2A binds the non-classical MHC molecule HLA-E and has been associated with inhibitory signaling.
The NKG2A-HLA-E axis is a target of cancer immunotherapy, and an anti-NKG2A antibody has been evaluated in combination regimens. Klrc1-deficient mice are viable with altered NK-cell responses.
applications: Humanized KLRC1 (NKG2A) models, in which the human receptor replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to evaluate NKG2A-directed agents in defined experimental settings.

why: Cd8a is the mouse ortholog of human CD8A and encodes the CD8 alpha chain, part of the CD8 co-receptor on cytotoxic T cells. CD8 binds MHC class I and has been associated with support of T-cell-receptor recognition and cytotoxic T-cell function.

CD8 T cells are central to antitumor and antiviral immunity, and CD8 is used as a marker and imaging target in immunotherapy research. Cd8a-deficient mice show impaired development of cytotoxic T cells.
applications: Humanized CD8A models, in which the human chain replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to study CD8 T-cell biology and to evaluate CD8-directed agents and imaging approaches in defined experimental settings.

why: Cdh17 is the mouse ortholog of human CDH17 and encodes cadherin-17 (LI-cadherin), a calcium-dependent cell-adhesion molecule expressed mainly in intestinal and related epithelia. Cadherin-17 has been associated with cell adhesion in the gut.

Cadherin-17 is expressed on gastrointestinal adenocarcinomas with limited expression in many normal tissues, and CDH17-directed approaches, including CAR T cells, are under study. Cdh17-deficient mice show changes in intestinal mineral handling.

why: Lgr5 is the mouse ortholog of human LGR5 and encodes a leucine-rich-repeat G-protein-coupled receptor that binds R-spondins and potentiates Wnt signaling. LGR5 marks stem cells in the intestine and other tissues and has been associated with tissue renewal.

LGR5 has been associated with cancer-stem-cell populations and treatment resistance in colorectal and other cancers, and LGR5-directed approaches are under study. Lgr5 reporter and lineage-tracing mice are widely used in stem-cell research.
applications: Humanized LGR5 models, in which the human receptor replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to evaluate LGR5-directed agents in defined experimental settings.
Lgr5 reporter mice are used to track and study stem cells.

why: Clec9a is the mouse ortholog of human CLEC9A and encodes CLEC9A (DNGR-1, CD370), a C-type lectin receptor expressed on a subset of dendritic cells. CLEC9A binds exposed actin filaments on dead cells and has been associated with cross-presentation of antigens.
CLEC9A is a target for directing antigens to dendritic cells in vaccine and immunotherapy approaches under study. Clec9a-deficient mice show altered cross-presentation of cell-associated antigens.

why: Fcer1a is the mouse ortholog of human FCER1A and encodes the alpha subunit of the high-affinity IgE receptor (FcεRI), which binds immunoglobulin E. The alpha subunit has been associated with IgE binding, and the receptor complex signals in mast cells and basophils.
FcεRI is central to IgE-mediated allergic responses, and the IgE pathway is targeted therapeutically. Fcer1a-deficient mice show loss of IgE-mediated mast-cell responses.
applications: Humanized FCER1A models, in which the human subunit replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to study IgE-mediated responses and to evaluate agents targeting the IgE pathway in defined experimental settings.

why: Ghrl is the mouse ortholog of human GHRL and encodes preproghrelin, which is processed into the acylated peptide hormone ghrelin (and obestatin). Ghrelin acts on the growth-hormone-secretagogue receptor and has been associated with stimulation of appetite and release of growth hormone.

Ghrelin has been associated with regulation of food intake and energy balance, and the ghrelin system is studied as a target for metabolic and appetite-related conditions. Ghrl-deficient mice are viable with modest metabolic phenotypes.
